title: Millaista: describing a substance
summary: Millaista asks what a substance is like. Millaista kahvi on? — Kahvi on kuumaa.
prerequisiteSkills: Millaisia and minkälaisia: describing several things
objectives: Ask what a substance is like with millaista.
Keep the substance subject basic and the descriptive adjective singular partitive.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.

Millaista asks what a substance is like. The question word is singular partitive; the substance subject stays in its basic form: Millaista kahvi on? (“What is the coffee like?”). Minkälaista is an alternative.
keyPoints: Do not use the countable-thing pattern automatically for a substance.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Describe the substance with a singular partitive adjective: Kahvi on kuumaa (“The coffee is hot”). The ending belongs to the describing adjective, not the subject. In the taught patterns, add -a/-ä to kuuma, kylmä, makea or hyvä.
A natural short reply to “Millaista kahvi on?” is “Kuumaa.” (“Hot.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
A substance description keeps its singular partitive adjective in this negative correction. The actual quality follows the rejected one.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use the singular partitive describing adjective while keeping the substance subject in its basic form.

kylmää means cold here. Kylmä + -ä gives singular partitive kylmää.
makeaa means sweet here. Makea + -a gives singular partitive makeaa.
hyvää means good here. Hyvä + -ä gives singular partitive hyvää.
